name: storage-quota-bucket-page
description: Modelled on a real message the engine originally scored 30/100 (caution) on a single content finding. Every deliberate choice in it defeats a different rule: the display name is spelled in mathematical sans-serif so no ASCII pattern matches it, the From domain sits under a TLD that does not exist, the payload is an HTML file in a public Google Cloud Storage bucket so the destination host is impeccable, the body forges a green 'trusted sender' notice, and 2,784 characters of unrelated prose sit inside an <object style="display:none"> to dilute the ratio of suspicious wording — which also diluted our own content rules, since bodyText came from textContent. An unsubscribe line and a link named 'unsubscribe' bought it the bulk-mail suppression on top. Recipient and sender labels invented, bucket and relay host renamed; storage.googleapis.com is kept because it is the finding. The service the message impersonates is unnamed in the original too: 'Cloud Secure Inc.' is the attacker's invention, not a real correspondent.
